cases.title: 3D helicopter scenes
cases.takeaway: Explore procedural helicopter modeling through two contrasting Three.js scenes.
cases.notes: SadAlbert10 asks for a realistic Mario-themed helicopter in Three.js without using an existing model. The paired clips show two different scene treatments: an airfield view and a forest helipad. The source labels the left result Astra 6/6.2 and the right Opus 5.5. Use the pair to compare the helicopter shape, environment and presentation against the same brief, while keeping the creator’s model labels and ordering intact.
cases.author: SadAlbert10

cases.title: Realistic PS5 controller SVG
cases.takeaway: Use a familiar product as a test of shape, shading and material detail.
cases.notes: SadAlbert10 presents a PS5 controller illustration as an SVG result, reporting a single attempt without a reference image. The public brief is short: make a realistic PS5 controller. The visible image combines a white shell, dark center grips, familiar buttons and soft shading. It is a useful visual-design example for examining recognizable geometry and product detail; the original post provides the image and the author’s description of the vector output.
cases.author: SadAlbert10

cases.title: A robot awakens in a hand-drawn forest
cases.takeaway: Turn a detailed scene brief into a short animated sequence.
cases.notes: Leo compares an ancient robot awakening and taking flight in a forest, with the upper sequence labeled Astra and the lower Fable 5.5. The public prompt asks for a hand-drawn 2D look and a single self-contained HTML deliverable, specifying lighting, movement and staging. The source credits Chetaslua for the Fable side and describes the Astra result as 6(6.2). Compare how each sequence interprets the same setting, story beat and visual direction.
cases.author: leo114119

cases.title: Pelican cycling around a vertical loop
cases.takeaway: Combine character motion, a bicycle and a looping three-dimensional track.
cases.notes: FiniYang’s first demonstration places a white pelican on a red bicycle above a coastal scene. The track rises into a vertical loop, and the sequence shows the rider upside down against an eclipsed sun before returning toward the bridge. This makes the clip useful for inspecting how character pose, bicycle orientation, track geometry and camera framing work together. Reposts and the later split-screen comparison of this same loop-track output are grouped with the original work.
cases.author: FiniYang
cases.what_it_shows: Bicycle motion on a vertical loop

cases.title: A semi-open-world 3D RPG
cases.takeaway: Inspect a small game world that combines a character, environment and interface.
cases.notes: FiniYang’s second demonstration is a semi-open-world role-playing game, described by the creator as made in one go. The footage shows a third-person character moving through stone ruins and vegetation, with a minimap, task text and action icons framing the scene. The clip brings together world-building and game-interface design in one visible result. Follow the original for the creator’s gameplay presentation and use the scene as a reference for the components of a compact RPG prototype.
cases.author: FiniYang

cases.title: Coastal Cruise: a 3D pelican cyclist
cases.takeaway: Present a character animation inside a compact scene-player interface.
cases.notes: Leo’s Coastal Cruise page shows a helmeted pelican on a green bicycle beside the sea and a lighthouse. Playback and speed controls sit below the scene, giving the result the feel of a small interactive exhibit. Leo reports roughly eleven minutes of work. The character, bicycle, coastal setting and page layout distinguish this 3D example from the separate hand-drawn cycling study. Inspect both the scene composition and the way the player presents the animation.
cases.author: leo114119

cases.title: The Pelican Cyclist: an illustrated seaside ride
cases.takeaway: Explore a flat illustrated treatment of the classic pelican-on-a-bicycle task.
cases.notes: Leo’s separate Pelican Cyclist example uses a hand-drawn seaside scene, a sunset, a lighthouse and a lightly textured color palette. A pause control and playback-speed options sit beneath the illustration. The work has a different visual language and page layout from Coastal Cruise, so it is retained as its own demonstration. Use it to compare how the same familiar subject can become either a dimensional character scene or a quieter illustrated motion study.
cases.author: leo114119

cases.title: A Japanese fantasy city in pixel art
cases.takeaway: Compare two interpretations of a detailed city-animation brief.
cases.notes: notjazii shares a split GIF of two Japanese-style waterfront cities, with castles, bridges, boats and a moonlit sky. The upper panel is labeled GPT-6.2 Astra and the lower GPT-6 Astra. The creator reports the same prompt, a single attempt and max reasoning for both. The newer run was made by a friend in Codex, while the earlier run used Devin. Keep that difference in host and operator alongside the visual comparison.
cases.author: notjazii

cases.title: An animated model introduction
cases.takeaway: Inspect a short motion-design piece built around abstract imagery and typography.
cases.notes: GulaGala001 shares a 24-second introduction and attributes its creation to gpt-6.2-astra. The clip combines a reflective abstract ring with changing introduction text, including an Every question frame. It extends the collection beyond game and character scenes into a compact promotional motion piece. Look at the relationship between the central graphic, contrast and typography in the published clip; the source does not specify a particular implementation or production method.
cases.author: GulaGala001

cases.title: Four models build an open-world RPG
cases.takeaway: Compare four game-scene treatments in one shared presentation.
cases.notes: noclipepe presents four RPG outputs in a single comparison video: GPT-6.2 Astra (?), Fable 5.5 (routing), Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1. The publisher describes a common prompt and contrasts the environments, lighting and gameplay presentation. The Astra panel shows bright ruins and a golem scene. Keep the question mark and routing label from the source when reading the comparison. The AI/ML API-branded video includes the publisher’s own ratings, rather than a controlled benchmark.
cases.author: noclipepe
